newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes strong, more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes strong, more gains expected.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended strong across the board after rising in the afternoon on light short-covering and fresh trade buying.
May closed up 30 stg at 1,002 stg per tonne and July gained 28 to 1,018.
Short-covering in London followed by some from locals in New York gave futures their initial boost, traders said.
Then, light trade buying emerged to help cocoa scale Tuesday and Wednesday's highs, they said. May hit a session high of 1,005 stg and July peaked at 1,019.
Switches were active, with July/September tightening from 16 this morning to about 10 in the afternoon. July/December also narrowed sharply.

The rise was seen as mostly technical after a few days of sharp declines. Traders said the market finally showed signs of fatigue on the downside after testing the week's lows several times with little follow-through.
They said funds also appeared sold out and origins already well-sold for their crop so neither is likely to pose any threat to higher aims.

Speculative selling or rolling of open May positions left in New York before first notice day there on April 17 is also expected to wind down, which would allow May to move up to 1,090 stg before the end of the month, traders said.
After Wednesday's trading, speculative May open interest at the CSCE fell 1,579 lots to 15,596.
Total LIFFE volume on Thursday was a healthy 10,161 contracts, with July grabbing 2,262 lots. December followed, notching 1,897 contracts and March 1998 was a close third with 1,879.
In options, July 1,100 calls traded 127 times, according to LIFFE.
